what: Regency Centers owns about 480 American shopping centres, most of them anchored by a supermarket, and leases the space to grocers, restaurants and local services.
customers: Supermarket chains, restaurants, medical and service tenants signing leases of five to twenty years.
money: tenants' share of taxes and maintenance, plus rent tied to sales
moat: Grocery anchors bring people to the centre every week, which makes the small shops around them want the space and willing to pay for it. Well-located grocery centres rarely come up for sale.
risks: $5.0B of debt against $121M of cash, so refinancing costs matter
A tenant bankruptcy leaves space empty and takes time to re-let
26 times earnings for a landlord growing rent in the low single digits
opportunities: A 34.0% net margin and $858M of free cash flow on $1.6B of revenue
Occupancy is near record levels and almost no new shopping centres are being built
Rents on expiring leases are being reset upward, which lifts income without new investment
watch: Leased occupancy and the rent spread on renewed leases.
